editorial_conventions.impact: 1-5 editorial: consequence for a mid-market supply chain org if the signal holds

meta.cadence_note: E07 covers a SIX-WEEK window (Aug 6 - Sep 17). No editions were published between E06 (W32) and E07 (W38). Pattern strength moves, signal counts and org tallies for E07 reflect six weeks of accumulation and are NOT comparable to a weekly delta.

patterns.title: From insight to execution: AI that acts, not advises
orgs: Kenco (3PL operator, agent count as operating plan)
patterns.verdict_1line: E07 (six-week window): sixth consecutive confirming edition, and the PACKAGING changed — agents now ship as catalogue items with job titles and a multi-week runtime (S01), while operators publish counts as operating plans (Kenco 6 live / 20 committed, S02; GE Appliances 800+, S03). FIRST MEASURED WEAKENER LOGGED: an interview study of 12 industrial companies puts 7 at assistant level, 4 at task-agent level, 1 at coordinated multi-agent, none above — and 4 hold capabilities they cannot deploy because output cannot be verified (S09). Capability is not the ceiling; verification is. Audited customer savings number still missing after SEVEN editions. SAP Outbound agent silent a SIXTH cycle (background watch).
confirmers: an audited customer autonomy or savings number (Siemens Erlangen operating results remain the strongest candidate)
a vendor disclosing the PAID share of an agent base separately from trials (Kinaxis S04 is the closest so far, combined at ~10%)
weakeners: MEASURED INSTANCE LOGGED E07 (S09): verification, not capability, caps deployment in 4 of 12 industrial companies. A second independent study finding the same would turn the ceiling into a wall.

patterns.title: The moat is business context, not the model
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: strongest evidence came from an OPERATOR not a vendor — GE Appliances' agents run on the company's own production data model, and the one result with a number (back orders -25% across 600+ suppliers) came from applying that context to ordinary clerical work (S03). Pattern's own confirmer STILL NOT FIRED: AVEVA + Cognite ($3.1B, announced Jun 30) remains pre-close with no packaging announced, so 'context' has never appeared as its own priced line item. Counter-evidence for the weakener: S09 found 11 of 12 industrial companies blocked by context capacity, which argues models are NOT getting good enough at raw-context reasoning.
confirmers: a context layer sold as its own priced SKU — AVEVA + Cognite packaging post-close remains the nearest candidate
weakeners: frontier models reasoning well enough over raw tables that definition layers stop mattering — no evidence; S09's context-capacity barrier (11 of 12) argues the other way

patterns.title: AI economics shift from seats to outcomes and tokens
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: clearest six weeks this pattern has had. Vendor-defined billing units became default vocabulary (Salesforce 'Agentic Work Units', 7B cumulative / 3.2B in Q2, S01; Acumatica 'AI Units', 5,000/mo in managed availability ~100 prompts, S08). Deloitte published revenue-recognition guidance for outcome-priced agentic AI products (Jun 4, S13) — audit guidance follows models being SOLD, the most reliable structural tell available. Published per-outcome rates now citable: Zendesk $1.50 committed / $2.00 PAYG; Intercom Fin $0.99, no charge when unresolved. Buy side moved too: Gartner tells CPOs to run AI as its own category with enterprise standards (Aug 18, S05). NOTE: prior org list double-counted Salesforce under two descriptions; merged in E07, so 9 -> 11 rather than 9 -> 12.
confirmers: a published price per AI Unit at Acumatica 2026 R2 — the mid-market tell, now waited on for five editions
outcome or per-unit terms appearing in any mid-market ERP quote
weakeners: outcome pricing reverting to consumption floors and minimums — read the fixed / metered / outcome-tied shares of every hybrid quote separately

patterns.title: Data readiness is the binding constraint
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: the constraint acquired a sharper name — not only whether the data is ready, but whether anyone can VERIFY what the agent did with it. 11 of 12 industrial companies could not get enough of their own context in front of a model at once; human review remained the only trusted check and does not scale (S09). Mirror image from a regulator: New York routed credit-delinquency reporting through the cannabis seed-to-sale rail effective Sep 15, fixing the quality of a future AI dataset via a one-business-day reporting habit established now (S14).
confirmers: settled enough to act on; the pilot template now carries a VERIFICATION gate (M24) above the adoption gate (M18)
weakeners: a wave of audited mid-market ROI results would soften the no-impact half of the consensus — none observed

patterns.title: The plumbing is standardizing: MCP + A2A move from experiment to default
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: the standard grew the layer governed buyers were waiting for — Enterprise-Managed Authorization reached STABLE, giving central control of agent-to-system access through the organisation's existing identity provider; Anthropic, Microsoft and Okta named as early adopters (S12). That removes the last structural objection to connecting AI to systems of record. Adoption figures circulating (not interchangeable): Stacklok survey 41% of software orgs in limited/broad production; an industry count at 28% of the largest enterprises within 18 months of publication; registry ~9,652 published servers (May 24). None measures quality. GAP UNCHANGED AND MORE CONSPICUOUS: after a partner conference given over to AI (Ascent, Aug 17-20), Acumatica announced no first-party connector (S08). WMS/TMS still silent. CAVEAT: S12 rests on implementer/secondary analysis; the spec repository was not read directly in this compile.
confirmers: a first-party connector from Acumatica at 2026 R2 (NetSuite set the reference posture)
the first first-party connectors from WMS / TMS vendors
weakeners: value migrating to proprietary layers built on top of the open core

patterns.title: Foundation forecasters are the new baseline — routing and hybrids win
orgs: Academic benchmark wave (2026: volatility, returns, multi-regime)
TIME benchmark authors (NTU / Griffith / Tsinghua / Datadog / Squirrel AI)
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: REPLICATION ARRIVED IN A STRONGER FORM THAN THE WATCH ASKED FOR — not a second retailer, but a contamination-free benchmark (TIME, arXiv 2602.12147v3, Mar 4): 50 freshly curated datasets, 98 tasks, 8 domains, strict zero-shot, built specifically to avoid pre-training leakage, which also answers the E06 evaluation-leakage warning by construction. Top-3 overall Chronos-2 / TimesFM-2.5 / TiRex on MASE and CRPS. CENTRAL RESULT = THIS PATTERN'S SECOND CLAUSE AS EVIDENCE: pattern-level rankings do NOT align with overall rankings — Chronos-2 leads stationary series, TimesFM-2.5 leads non-stationary, Toto 3rd non-stationary -> 6th stationary. No single model to buy; routing is the design decision. Two cautions carried: weak-seasonality series cluster ~0.7 MASE (choice barely matters); high-variation series draw near-flat forecasts that still score competitively. CONFLICT NAMED: Datadog co-authorship with Toto in the evaluated field. Preprint, not peer-reviewed.
confirmers: a planning vendor exposing model choice as a control rather than a hidden default
a second demand-domain replication at an operator (Alibaba E06 remains the only one)
weakeners: a next-generation model decisively closing the gap across EVERY series type, which would make routing unnecessary

patterns.title: AI is a demand-side force: the compute buildout moves freight, power and components
orgs: Kinaxis (data-centre build-outs named as a demand vertical)
patterns.verdict_1line: E07: the pattern got its UNIT OF MEASURE — ~100,000 truckloads per gigawatt of new US data-centre capacity, against ~50 GW announced for 2026-27 (~5M incremental truckloads); flatbed and heavy-haul spot at multi-year highs; construction spend ~$41B/yr (S06). It also got its EXPIRY DATE from the same sources: only ~1/3 of the 2026 pipeline under active construction, ~half of announcements expected to slip or cancel, 18-24 month construction clock, sharp post-completion drop-off. AIR SIDE — read carefully: August spot $3.13/kg, +24% YoY vs the +38-41% reported in E06, demand +6%; but Xeneta REVISED ITS FULL-YEAR OUTLOOK UP to +5-15% on long-term contract rates. The YoY compression is a BASE EFFECT, not a price decline, and therefore does NOT count as the correction tripwire (S07). E06's 'first candidate data point' should be read with that correction. Demand also appeared on a software income statement: Kinaxis named data-centre build-outs as a growth vertical (S04).
confirmers: carrier and trucking results quantifying AI-cargo share
weakeners: two consecutive months of falling ABSOLUTE spot levels with stable capacity — note the E07 year-on-year compression is a base effect and is NOT this signal
the share of the announced pipeline actually breaking ground falling materially below ~1/3

watch_items.item: SAP Outbound Task Orchestration Agent GA — silent a SIXTH straight cycle (E02-E07). Remains on background watch; report only on news.
Fabric planning GA rollout completion. E07: nothing observed — seventh silent cycle. Consider retiring or re-scoping if silent again.

Acumatica 2026 R2 — the single most consequential date on the internal roadmap. THREE OPEN QUESTIONS: (a) the R2 RELEASE DATE itself is not published in any partner material reviewed for E07; (b) price per AI Unit (AI Assistant goes GA/purchasable at R2; managed-availability allocation is 5,000 units/month ~100 prompts); (c) still no first-party MCP connector. AI Document Intelligence for AP previewed for R2 (overlaps the M15 freight-audit parsing half). AcuChat GA and AI Studio as a standalone product confirmed at Ascent 2026 (Aug 17-20).

AVEVA + Cognite ($3.1B, announced Jun 30) packaging post-close: does 'context' become its own priced line item (P2's only confirmer)? E07: still pre-close, no packaging news. Two consecutive quiet editions on this item — apply the quiet-cycle rule at E08.

Q3/Q4 earnings-call language check: agents re-described as 'assistants' (P1 weakener)? E07 reads run the other way (Kinaxis agents in 'nearly every' major new agreement; Salesforce shipping named role-agents). Kinaxis Q2 CLOSED — read as E07 S04.

P7 validation: carrier/trucking results quantifying AI-cargo share; spread to ocean freight. E07 added the per-gigawatt rate (~100k truckloads/GW) and the expiry structure (~1/3 of pipeline under construction, ~50% slippage estimate). CORRECTION TRIPWIRE RESTATED: two consecutive months of falling ABSOLUTE air spot levels with stable capacity — the E07 year-on-year compression (+24% vs +38-41%) is a BASE EFFECT and does not qualify; Xeneta raised its full-year contract outlook to +5-15%.

Agent-platform pricing: a vendor-published mid-market price list for a SUPPLY CHAIN agent. E07: per-outcome prices exist but only in customer service (Zendesk $1.50/$2.00; Intercom $0.99) — no supply-chain-priced comparable anywhere. Both role-plays flagged this gap.

P6 follow-through: E07 confirmer fired via the TIME benchmark (contamination-free, 50 datasets / 98 tasks / 12 models). REMAINING GAPS: (a) a second demand-domain replication at an operator; (b) planning vendors exposing model-routing controls rather than one hidden embedded model. Quiet-cycle counter at 0.

Cannabis lens: ACTIVE again in E07 after one zero edition (S14 — NY routes credit-delinquency reporting through Metrc effective Sep 15; bulletin NY_IB_025 Sep 8). NOTE: S14 is a regulatory/data-architecture change, not an AI product launch — the sweep still found no qualifying AI ANNOUNCEMENT in the window. Standing questions carried: the 40-60% AI-influenced-transactions projection (E05 S11) still unmeasured; Metrc-class rail owners shipping first-party AI (now more interesting, since the rail holds payment behaviour).
Siemens Erlangen 'fully AI-driven factory' (from 2026): watch for published operating results — still the strongest possible P1 confirmer. E07: nothing observed.

NEW E07: Salesforce 'Marshall' supply-chain agent — no published functional detail beyond the role name. Watch for (a) what it actually does, (b) whether the long-horizon runtime spreads beyond the sales agent, (c) whether the Nov GA date for the sales agent holds, (d) whether rivals answer with named role-agents and per-unit-of-work pricing in Q4.

NEW E07: Kenco's 20-agent commitment — clock runs from the Aug 5 partnership. Watch the interim count and, critically, any DISCLOSED service-level or cost movement. Six agents live with no audited number attached is the pattern's recurring shape.

NEW E07: verification tooling as a product category — output verification, evidence trails, conformance checking sold rather than bundled. S09 says human review is the only trusted check and does not scale; the verdict box notes nobody is selling the alternative yet. First vendor to price it is a significant signal.

NEW E07 (product debt, from role-play): tier T1 is labelled 'Analyst / peer-reviewed research' but E07 files two arXiv PREPRINTS (S09, S10) there. Either add a preprint tier or relabel T1. Also: assertions.js line ~114 still hardcodes "search 'stateless' finds S12" — the MCP card must stay at code S12 and contain 'stateless' until that assertion is generalised.

lessons: Role-play persona must state reader tech fluency explicitly; defaults drift to the builder's level (E01 draft-1 failure).
Glossary (TERMS) and Stack-detail line are template-level; append terms, never strip the layer.
Check publisher families before setting multi:true.
Timeline right-hand markers are third-party forecasts, label as such.

Template Rev E (Jul 3): dual REGISTERS — write exec copy (xone/xwhy) separately from analyst copy for every signal; palette bound to view (warm exec / cool analyst, green brand accent); DELTA object + pattern move chips power the weekly pulse strip; append weekly item to feed.xml; update data-ed numeral; PWA assets (icons/manifest/sw) are permanent — never remove.

Rev F editorial rules (Jul 3): never embed UI pills in running prose; badges nowrap; 62ch reading measures; one green data accent; app icon = approved radar-sweep mark (no redesign/recolor without sign-off); 390px mobile checklist incl. notch clearance runs every edition.

Taxonomy v2 + cannabis lens (Jul 3, Rev G): six locked keys (plan/source/make/deliver/sell/infra); value-chain ribbon + infrastructure foundation band replace filter chips; every research week sweeps all 5 stages + infra + cannabis industry; cann:true signals feed the conditional Industry Lens section (auto-hidden when none qualify); stage-focus line must show honest thin/empty states.

E02 (Jul 9, unattended): mimic-board 'from' links must reference current-edition signal codes — board is edition-scoped (M7-M12), while open_actions in state carries all editions; role-play subagent caught exec-register mechanics leakage in shared 'what' blocks (S12/S13) — shared blocks must pass the exec bar too, since both registers render them.

E03 (Jul 16, unattended): role-play subagents caught (a) date-logic errors in forward-looking copy — check every 'next edition confirms X' claim against the actual calendar (a Jul 23 edition cannot confirm a Jul 28 ship); (b) orphan numbers referencing prior editions ($262B) — attribute cross-edition figures explicitly; (c) internal shorthand (Onematica, SADA) needs TERMS glosses since every edition has potential first-time readers; (d) the scatter caption had a hardcoded signal range (S01-S15) — now genericized, keep it generic; (e) assertions.js still hardcodes 'search stateless finds S12' — keep the MCP-spec card at code S12 (or generalize the assertion when next editing the harness is authorized).

E04 (Jul 23, unattended): role-play caught a WEEKDAY error repeated 6x in the marquee signal (called Jul 28 'Monday'; it is Tuesday) — verify the weekday of every dated claim against a calendar before shipping; date arithmetic ('five days out') can be right while the weekday is wrong.

E04: compile-machinery narration ('this compile ran it', 'surfaced by this week's sweep', 'the card is conservatively single-source') in shared 'what' blocks reads as production mechanics to the exec register — keep provenance honesty, but phrase it in reader terms; detailed provenance lives in the Method box.

E04: TAKES must be business-consequence framed in both registers — an IT-status takeaway ('validate servers against the spec') fails the exec CEO-retell test; the freight-cost story beat it for the third slot. Bare M-code chains (M11 → M3) don't belong in exec-visible surfaces.
E04: P7 added — first pattern-set change; procedure held (E03 candidate flag → multi-source corroboration → Method-box note). Two-cycle candidate rule feels right for pattern additions.

E05 (Jul 30, unattended): the two-quiet-cycles rule fired mid-build (P3) and the resulting deep-dive changed the edition (S13 added after first verification pass). Run the quiet-cycle count during step 0, before research ends — deep-dives belong in the research phase, not the fix loop.

E05: role-play caught a stat quoted with its source's own loose arithmetic ('doubling' for 22%→58%). Recompute every ratio in copy even when the source's framing is being quoted; state the numbers instead of the multiplier when in doubt.

E05: exec-register leakage recurred in shared 'what' blocks on the two most technical cards (S12/S10 first drafts read like release notes). For infrastructure signals, draft the shared 'what' in business language FIRST and push every mechanism to the tech line; the exec bar applies to shared blocks (E02 lesson) and infrastructure cards are where it breaks.

E06: the pulse strip claimed 'P6 + P7 confirmers fire' when P7's event was a promotion, not a confirmer — promotions and confirmer firings are different events; label them precisely in DELTA items.

E06: P7 promoted forming->hardening — second pattern-lifecycle change; promotion bar used: >=3 corroborated cycles + spread across >=3 evidence classes + ~2x org count. Reuse this bar.

RECOMPUTE EVERY INTERVAL AND ORDINAL in copy against the underlying dates before shipping.
